text: Never put Stack.useSync on a single resource prop field (e.g. domain: Stack.useSync(...)). Alchemy Plan.resolveInput does not unwrap nested Effects, so the Effect object is sent to Cloudflare as hostname and deploy fails with SchemaError. Wrap the entire props object: Worker(id, Stack.useSync(({ stage }) => ({ ... })), impl).
prescription: Wrap entire InputProps object in Stack.useSync; set domain: stage === "prod" ? HOST : undefined inside.

text: Cloudflare Worker + SPA assets must set runWorkerFirst for /api/* (and /ingest). Without it, notFoundHandling single-page-application serves index.html for Better Auth callbacks; AuthBoundary then redirects to /auth?next=/api/auth/callback/google?code=… and OAuth never completes.
Bound streaming persistence and diagnostic writes with an explicit per-generation operation budget; reserve terminal-state capacity before optional replay data.
Do not replace client-generated chat message IDs during persistence; preserve validated incoming IDs so retry, edit, and branch operations address the stored message.
Never deploy a Worker that references new tables until its generated D1 migration has been applied and verified in production.
When deleting the active chat, finish the route redirect before broadcasting the sidebar refresh so the UI cannot retain a deleted conversation.
Avoid duplicating generic application source as string templates. Keep canonical files in generic fixtures; generator must materialize them with explicit configuration substitutions.
Avoid coupled chat session transitions implemented as multiple independent React state setters. Model session state and transitions in one reducer or state machine.
Avoid chat lifecycle state in React reducers; model durable chat transitions with an explicit XState machine exported from @emi/core/web.
Never emit a request event as the success event for an actor operation; use a distinct typed completion event so parent routing cannot repeat the request.
Never render external or persisted URLs directly into href or src; route every sink through an allow-list policy appropriate to the URL and media type.
Never spread caller-controlled transport body fields after transport-owned identifiers or mode flags; reserve protected keys at the boundary.
Every replaceable async actor query must carry an operation identity and ignore stale success or failure before mutating parent state.
Keep each actor-owned side effect on one routed path; do not retain a dead duplicate callback or direct action for the same operation.
Admit a durable chat generation before persisting its incoming user turn, or make both operations one rollback-safe transaction; never leave admission races with orphan turns.
Keep product-domain HTTP contracts out of @emi/core; generic core exports only foundational contracts and flavor packages compose product APIs over CoreApi.

Do not expose a flat public utility barrel or wildcard public export. Group related operations under a domain class or owned instance; individually export only independently consumable React view primitives.
Do not keep compatibility aliases or migration-only packages in the final source tree; migrate consumers to the target public contract and delete the alias.
Never use index.ts as an internal module or import target; flatten implementation files and reserve explicit .export.ts files for package subpath boundaries.
Do not re-export symbols with export-from syntax; a public boundary must own its curated bindings and name the domain it exposes.
Effect services and server adapters must be provided through Context.Service and Layer composition; do not instantiate use cases or repositories with constructor DI.
Keep generic chat view behavior in @emi/core; application packages may provide product renderers and configuration, but must not own generic thread, scroll, or message primitives.
Do not create forwarding modules that only re-export another package or file; import the owning domain directly or implement a named adapter boundary.
prescription: Delete the forwarding module and import the owning package or explicit implementation.

text: Generic protocol and server contracts must not import raw database, Cloudflare, or AI SDK types; keep platform details in advanced database and adapter boundaries.
prescription: Define a generic port/DTO and map platform rows at the adapter boundary.

text: Do not use wildcard exports; name every public binding explicitly so the contract remains discoverable and reviewable.
prescription: Import the symbols locally and export an explicit list.

text: Server and adapter classes may have parameterless private constructors for static domains, but dependency-bearing construction must use Effect Context.Service and Layer.
prescription: Move dependencies into a Context.Service and compose them with Layer.

text: Do not create internal forwarding classes whose static fields only alias another domain; use the owning grouped domain directly. Public .export.ts facades are the explicit exception.
prescription: Delete the wrapper and import the owning domain directly; keep grouping only in the named public .export.ts boundary.

text: Keep each domain API under a named class or owned instance; do not expose a flat file of many unrelated runtime functions or mutable values. Exceptions require a documented independently consumable contract such as a schema, HTTP API item, React view primitive, or explicit .export.ts facade.
prescription: Create a domain owner with scoped static methods or instantiate it with injected services; keep implementation helpers private and expose only the smallest public surface.

text: Do not read ambient time, randomness, global fetch, browser storage, or browser state inside actor/use-case code; preserve deterministic injected dependencies and keep platform defaults at explicit adapter edges.
prescription: Add clock, ID, fetch, storage, or browser capabilities to the owning actor/service and provide defaults only in the platform adapter or app composition.

text: Generic Effect ports and use cases must return typed Effect or Stream programs. Promise or synchronous execution belongs only to named HTTP, browser, or platform adapters.
Actor-owned state must not be mirrored in React useState or useReducer. React subscribes to the actor runtime and dispatches commands through the view facade.
Internal files must not forward or re-export types from another module; only named package or subpath export boundaries may curate imports and exports.
Static-only domain classes must be named classes with static methods and no empty private constructor; dependency-bearing services belong in Effect Context.Service and Layer.

Generic core domain owners must be ordinary named classes; do not use abstract classes for public grouping or dependency contracts. Use Effect Context.Service and Layer for dependency-bearing services.
prescription: Replace the abstract class with a named static domain class or an Effect Context.Service composed by Layer.

reason: The clean-slate boundary bans empty private constructors; static domains need no constructor and dependency-bearing services use Effect Context.Service and Layer.

reason: Malformed rule record created by an argument-order mistake; replaced with the intended Effect service-facade rule.
Malformed rule record created by an argument-order mistake; replaced with the intended Effect context-composition rule.
Malformed rule record created by an argument-order mistake; replaced with the intended typed-error handling rule.

text: Effect service values must be yielded once inside an Effect program; do not build static service-operation facades with repeated Effect.flatMap(ServiceKey, ...).
prescription: Yield the Context.Service once in Effect.gen, return an implementation object from Layer.effect, and reuse the local service value.

text: Do not capture Effect.context only to re-provide it or a database Layer through local provideContext/provideDatabase wrappers; compose Layers once and keep platform context conversion at the outer boundary.
prescription: Provide a service Layer once or construct the adapter at the platform edge; keep nested Effects environment-aware instead of rebinding the same context repeatedly.

text: When an Effect failure is a tagged domain error, handle it with Effect.catch or Effect.catchTag and preserve the typed error channel; do not use catchIf as a replacement for typed Effect errors.
prescription: Use Schema.TaggedErrorClass or Data.TaggedError and match the _tag through Effect.catchTag, or use Effect.catch with an explicit typed branch.

text: Do not pass a readable stream error through unchanged; map Stream.fromReadableStream onError causes into a tagged domain error so the Effect failure channel stays typed.
prescription: Map the cause to a Schema.TaggedErrorClass or Data.TaggedError in the adapter boundary.

text: Map Stream.fromReadableStream onError causes into a tagged domain error; do not leak raw unknown failures into the Effect error channel.
prescription: Use a Schema.TaggedErrorClass or Data.TaggedError mapper at the readable-stream boundary and keep the stream failure typed.

reason: The nested Stream.fromReadableStream context is enforced by the custom Oxlint rule emi/no-untyped-readable-stream-error; the ast-grep pattern was not sufficiently context-aware.

text: Fallible database and adapter queries in generic Effect domains must not use Effect.promise or declare a QueryDatabaseClient failure channel as never; use QueryDatabase.tryPromise or an equivalent tagged domain error, then map the failure at the owning domain boundary.
Use every named Effect Schema declaration through a decoder or exported contract; delete unused schema values.
prescription: Remove the declaration or route it through the owning contract.

text: Do not duplicate identical inline Effect Schema expressions in one module; name the schema once and reuse it.
prescription: Declare one named schema beside its owning contract and reuse it at each boundary.

text: Do not wrap pure Effects in providers or nest Effect provider wrappers; provide a service layer once at the boundary.
prescription: Yield the service inside the Effect program and compose one layer at the outer adapter.

text: Test-only effect execution aliases that merely call Effect.runPromise add no value; call Effect.runPromise at the assertion or setup boundary so the execution boundary stays visible.
Test database fixtures must execute generated Drizzle schema statements; do not duplicate a schemaDdl or raw CREATE TABLE definition in tests.
Tool parameter contracts must be Effect Schema values; do not hand-write JSON Schema objects when Tool.make or Tool.dynamic can derive the wire schema.
Keep UI-message validation under the Chat.messages domain; do not export validateUIMessagesEffect or validateStoredUIMessagesEffect as flat helpers.
Do not render model-provided dynamic component specs through Schema.Unknown; decode the core dynamic-component schema and render only registered components.
Every chat stream transport must enforce an injected or configurable inactivity deadline and surface a typed terminal failure; a readable stream must not wait forever.
Every replaceable chat stream operation must verify it is still current before emitting completion or failure state; stale streams may not report success into a newer session.
Only an active send stream may mark an assistant as failed; idle UI errors must not cause a completed assistant to be removed on the next request.
Completion hooks must use the current stream message identity; never infer a new completion from the last historical assistant message.
Persisted message revisions and retries must validate connectivity and model credentials before mutating history or starting generation.
Optional suggestion side effects must not convert a completed chat stream into a failed stream when adapter metadata is missing or invalid.

Do not pass Context.Service-backed database, reader, writer, store, or repository dependencies through an Effect.fn input; yield the service inside Effect.gen and provide its Layer only at the adapter boundary.
